But there's only one node, and the pod anti-affinity requires pods to be on different hostnames — with only one node, a second pod cannot be scheduled (unschedulable). So the new ReplicaSet pod is Pending because of the requiredDuringScheduling podAntiAffinity on kubernetes.io/hostname.

That's the bug: the deployment template has required pod anti-affinity for all pods labeled app=app, which in a single-node cluster makes it impossible to run more than one replica at a time (and during rollout, new pods can't schedule). The old RS pods are on that node too? Actually old pods are Running. Hmm, the deployment was updated; the old pods are from the previous ReplicaSet. So the current state: 3 old pods running on same node. New pod can't be scheduled due to anti-affinity with those pods (same hostname). That's why "unschedulable" in cluster name.

Fix: remove the podAntiAffinity from the deployment template. But is there another issue? The pending pod needs to become Ready. Let me check the pod spec details, events, and whether there's a service/rollout. Also maybe readiness probe? Image nginx:1.31.5 — does that tag exist? If image pull fails, it would be ImagePullBackOff, not Pending. The pending is Unscheduled.

So removing requiredDuringScheduling pod anti-affinity should let new pods schedule on the same node. Then all 3 replicas ready. Let's verify pending pod conditions and events first.
